slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: In weakly acid medium iron is released from transferrin; ascorbic acid reduces it to the ferrous (Fe2+) form.
Ferrous ions give a coloured complex with FerroZine; the colour intensity is proportional to the iron concentration.
Iron deficiency causes iron-deficiency anaemia; high iron is seen in haemochromatosis, cirrhosis, hepatitis. Day-to-day variation is marked in healthy people.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Iron-FZ” kit (IFU BSIS24-I, 08/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or heparinised plasma free of haemolysis, separated from the cells quickly; 7 days at 2–8 °C.
R1 — acetate buffer pH 4.9 100 mmol/L; R2 — reductant (ascorbic acid 99.7%); R3 — colour reagent (FerroZine 40 mmol/L); standard — iron 100 µg/dL.
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 562 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes; disposable ware is recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: dissolve one tube of R2 (reductant) in one bottle of R1 (buffer); cap and mix gently.
Working reagent stability: 3 months at 2–8 °C or 1 month at 15–25 °C. R3 is added separately.
Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 562 nm ≥ 0.020.
If glassware is used, soak it for 6 h in diluted HCl (20% v/v), rinse thoroughly with distilled water and dry.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
The values come from the SPINREACT “Iron-FZ” IFU (BSIS24-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 562 nm (530–590); temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Reagent blank: working reagent 1.0 mL + R3 1 drop + distilled water 200 µL. Standard: working reagent 1.0 mL + R3 1 drop + standard 200 µL.
4. Sample blank: working reagent 1.0 mL + sample 200 µL (no R3). Sample: working reagent 1.0 mL + R3 1 drop + sample 200 µL.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Mix and incubate: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at room temperature.
6. Read the absorbance of the standard and sample against the reagent blank; the colour is stable for at least 30 minutes.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: iron programme
rows: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at room temperature

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Iron (µg/dL) = [(A sample − A sample blank) − A reagent blank] / (A standard − A reagent blank) × 100.
Conversion: µg/dL × 0.179 = µmol/L.
Linear up to 1000 µg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.
IFU reference: men 65–175 µg/dL (11.6–31.3 µmol/L), women 40–150 µg/dL (7.16–26.85 µmol/L); reference values are strongly method-dependent.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Haemolysed samples are rejected: red cells contain iron and falsely raise the result.
Iron-contaminated ware gives falsely high results — use disposable ware or HCl-treated glassware.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: R1: H302 — harmful if swallowed; H315 — skin irritation; H319 — serious eye irritation.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
